deadline.value: Complete your application by December 9, 2026 for autumn 2027 entry (autumn only).
deadline.quote: Applications must be complete by December 9, 2026 for admission the following autumn.

gre_subject.value: The admissions page does not mention the Mathematics GRE.

toefl_min.value: To be admitted with financial support (TA funding), non-native speakers need TOEFL iBT 92+ plus speaking 26+ on TOEFL or 7.0+ speaking on IELTS; do not apply if you do not meet this.
toefl_min.quote: a score of 92 or higher on the TOEFL-iBT and either a score of at least 26 on the speaking section of the TOEFL-iBT or else a score of at least 7.0 on the speaking section of the IELTS. | You should not apply if you do not meet the English language requirement.

english_waiver.value: An Indian degree does not exempt you: the department's English-speaking-country list excludes India, so you need TOEFL 92+ with the speaking minimum.
english_waiver.quote: a Bachelor's degree from an institution in an English-speaking country listed in Memo #15/Policy 5.2 (note that the University's list of English-speaking countries is quite limited and does not include, for example, India or Hong Kong)

fee_waiver.value: Need-based waivers are for US applicants only; department waivers exist only for Math Alliance and MSRI-UP participants.
fee_waiver.quote: International applicants are not eligible for need-based fee waivers. | The Math Department offers fee waivers for Math Alliance Predoctoral Scholars and participants in MSRI-UP.

supervisor.value: The admissions page does not say whether you need a supervisor before admission.

funding.value: Graduate students are supported mainly through teaching assistantships; most are TA-funded, some RA or fellowship-funded.
funding.quote: Most of our students are funded by teaching assistantships (TA's), some are funded by research assistantships (RA's), and some have fellowships from outside of UW. | Our graduate students are supported through teaching assistantships.

entry_route.value: A bachelor's (not necessarily in maths) with advanced algebra and real analysis is enough; master's holders are also welcome.
entry_route.quote: Advanced undergraduate courses in both of the following subjects are required for admission to the PhD track. | We welcome students who have already taken graduate courses or who already have Master's degrees.

notes: UW also runs a separate PhD in Applied Mathematics (Department of Applied Mathematics), not covered here.
